subject: Cross-border controls & audit packet — next steps
messages:
From: Ana López <ana.lopez@bancus.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Krishna Singh <krishna.singh@bancus.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Cross-border controls & audit packet — next steps

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Bancus is moving quickly on the procurement track and our legal/compliance team has a few concrete asks before we can sign: a short packet showing the controls around cross-border transfers, evidence for GDPR Art. 28/30 (processing records + subprocessors table), and an ability to support a DPIA session with our data protection officer.

Specifically, can you provide: 
- A one‑page summary of where customer data may cross borders (regions/hyperlink to controls)
- A current subprocessors inventory with dates and transfer mechanisms (SCCs/MTAs)
- A short sample of processing ledger entries (redacted acceptable) and an explanation of retention windows
- Confirmation we can get a 2‑hour DPIA workshop and an example scope/agenda

We attached our standard vendor questionnaire; if you can fill the security/compliance sections and return by EOD Friday (2026-11-13) that would be ideal. We also need an initial statement of the legal basis used for processing and whether Redwood relies on any EU adequacy or SCCs for transfers.

Appreciate quick alignment — once legal signs off we can move the SOW to procurement.

Best,
Ana
Ana López
Head of Vendor Risk — Bancus Financial
[Attachment: Bancus_vendor_questionnaire.pdf (PDF)]

Action items:
1) Marissa: can you prepare a redacted ledger excerpt + subprocessors CSV and a short paragraph on retention policy by Thu 11/12?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ana López <ana.lopez@bancus.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-border controls & audit packet — next steps

Hi Ana — following up with the artifacts we can share immediately. Attached is a redacted excerpt of our processing ledger (CSV) showing sample entries, timestamps, processing categories, and which subprocessor handled the activity. Notes: PII is masked, and entries are sampled across three customer regions to demonstrate cross-border patterns.

Quick answers inline to your asks:
- Cross-border summary: We host model inference endpoints in eu‑west and us‑east by default; traffic that crosses regions is logged and routed per customer routing policy. Detailed region mapping is in the DPA packet (see Laura's link).
- Subprocessors: included in the CSV; columns indicate transfer mechanism (SCC / adequacy) and last attested date.
- Retention: operational logs retained 90 days, KV cache snapshots retained 14 days unless customer-specific retention override is requested; long‑term telemetry aggregated and retained for 24 months.

Attachments here: redacted_processing_ledger_excerpt.csv (sample), subprocessors_snapshot_20261112.csv (full inventory available under NDA).

If you want a larger sample or unredacted entries for audit review, we'll need a confidentiality addendum (we can provide one).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Privacy & Compliance Program Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
[Attachment: redacted_processing_ledger_excerpt.csv]

2) Evidence bundle: a staged bundle is available in our shared drive. It contains: current DPA, processing ledger sample (redacted), subprocessors inventory (attested), SCC templates, and KMS architecture diagram. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/bancus-privacy-packet

3) DPIA workshop: We propose Tue 2026-11-17 at 10:00 UTC — Connor please confirm with Ana. Workshop agenda attached to the drive (DPIA_workshop_agenda.md).

4) Audit access: for unredacted logs or larger samples we require an NDA + confidentiality addendum; we can provide a short template.

Please review the DPA amendment and evidence bundle. If signoff is fast, we can run the DPIA next week and get procurement moving.

Laura Bennett
